div.head: Becwæð 3.1
div.ab: butan ðæt læste ða hwile ðe ic libbe; forðam ni[s æni m]an on life, ðe æfre gehyrde, ðæt man cwydde oððon crafode hine on hundrede oððon ahwar on gemote, on ceapstowe oþþe on cyricware, ða hwile þe he lifde: unsac he wæs on life; beo on legere, swa swa he mote!

butan þæt læste ða hwile ðe ic libbe; forðam nis æt tinan on life, ðe æfre gehyrde, þæt man cwydde oððon crafode hine on hunræde oððon ahwar on gemote, on ceapstowe oðe on cyricware, ða hwile þe he lifede: unsac he wæs on life; beo on legere, swa swa he mote!

Sondern dies bleibe, so lange ich leben werde; denn nicht ist jemand am Leben, der je gehört hätte, dass jener in Anspruch genommen oder belangt worden sei in Hundertschaft oder irgendwo im Gericht, an Marktplatz oder in Kirchengemeinde, so lange er lebte: unverklagt war er im Leben; sei er im Grabe so [unangefochten,] wie er berechtigt ist.

But let this remain as long as I live; for there is no one alive who ever heard that he was claimed against or sued in the hundred or anywhere in a court, in the market-place or in the church congregation, as long as he lived: unaccused he was in life; let him be so [unchallenged] in the grave as he has the right.

except that it may last as long as I live. For there is no man alive who ever heard that it was claimed or craved in hundred or any other meeting, in market-place or church-congregation as long as he lived: uncontested he was in life, let him be so in his grave as he has every reason.

div.note: Some of Liebermann’s notes here are cut off in the gutter of the scan used, and are still to be completed.

U: translator probably Wormald, The Making of English Law (named in the original spreadsheet’s sub-header rows): check; B's ‘æt tinan’ should be corrected as in H (‘ni[s æni m]an’); H reads ‘nise tinan’. B's ‘hunræde’ and ‘oðe’ stand so. Liebermann compares II Cn 72.

note.seg: Diese Bed. ‘sondern’ in Ælfreds Boethius 15 und 17 [ed. Sedgefield p. 33. 40], zitiert von Toller Suppl. Price und Cockayne übs. ‘except’ sinnlos
This meaning ‘but (rather)’ in Ælfred’s Boethius 15 and 17 [ed. Sedgefield p. 33. 40], cited by Toller Suppl. Price and Cockayne translate ‘except’, which makes no sense
Vgl. Gl Erbnehmer 2a; ‘jener’ ist der Erblasser
Cf. Gl Erbnehmer 2a; ‘that man’ is the testator
